description:
gh:#54 https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/54 carries the full scope.

GOAL. A Haiku agent goes from 'settle a bed of pebbles' to 'k-eff of that bed' in one short script, using REAL DEM packings rather than an idealised arrangement. Every piece exists; none of the joins do.

EXISTS: granular DEM in outram-park-fork-liggghts (Simulation::new/step/run, Particle, contact mechanics, boundaries, mesh walls, thermal); sphere packing in mc pebble_beds::sphere_packing (CRP, pack_spheres, PackedSpheres); Woodcock/delta tracking for doubly-heterogeneous media (Majorant, DeltaFlight); stochastic media sampled rather than stored (CLS, SCLS); TrisoParticle::into_geometry() for ONE particle; run_keff_csg for general CSG.

THREE MISSING JOINS.
  1. DEM -> packing. outram-mc-libs does not depend on outram-park-fork-liggghts and there is no bridge. A settled Simulation holds positions; nothing turns them into Vec<Sphere> or PackedSpheres.
  2. Packing -> Geometry. PackedSpheres exposes is_inside_kernel(Position) — an IMPLICIT query for delta tracking — but has no conversion to CSG Geometry, so a packing cannot reach run_keff_csg.
  3. Double heterogeneity. into_geometry() gives CSG for one TRISO particle. Nothing composes N pebbles each containing M TRISO.

THE SCOPING DECISION THIS FORCES. 'General CSG' CANNOT mean explicit CSG for a whole core. HTR-10 is ~27,000 pebbles at ~11,000 TRISO each, order 3e8 particles. Explicit surfaces there are not slow, they are impossible — delta_tracking's own docs say surface tracking is 'ruinously expensive when there are O(10^5) boundaries along a path', and stochastic/ exists because 'a pebble holds O(10^4) fuel kernels and a core O(10^5) pebbles'.

So the workflow is HYBRID and the split must be explicit in the API rather than discovered: pebble centres -> EXPLICIT CSG (thousands of spheres is tractable and is what DEM produces); TRISO inside a pebble -> IMPLICIT via delta-tracking majorant or chord-length sampling. A tier-1 entry point picks the split; tier-2 allows override. What must not happen is an agent cheerfully assembling 1e8 CSG cells because the API permitted it.

STEPS. (1) packing_from_dem: Simulation -> Vec<Sphere>/PackedSpheres; needs a feature-gated dependency edge mc-libs -> liggghts, or a shared plain-data type so neither depends on the other — CHECK THE ANDROID/TERMUX RULE before adding the edge. (2) pebble_bed_geometry: packing -> Geometry, pebbles explicit, TRISO implicit via Majorant; RETURNS A REAL Geometry so it composes with every runner — the into_geometry() pattern, not the mc_keff_of_actinide_sphere trap. (3) Verify against keff_delta, which already does doubly-heterogeneous k-eff: the new route must agree within statistics on the same packing or one of them is wrong. (4) Verify packing statistics: a DEM bed and a CRP bed at the same nominal packing fraction should agree within statistics; if not, that is a real result about packing structure, but it must be MEASURED not assumed either way. (5) Compute budget: pebble count, particles x generations, wall-clock ceiling — a DEM settle plus a doubly-heterogeneous k-eff is the most expensive thing in this scoping set.

WHY DEM RATHER THAN CRP. CRP gives a packing at a target fraction; DEM gives one gravity and contact mechanics actually produce, including wall effects and the near-wall porosity oscillation that is a real pebble-bed feature and a known influence on bypass flow. Whether it moves k-eff is step 4's job.

Related: op-375p / gh:#41, op-wpi0 / gh:#43, op-jyyp (HTR-10), op-t3l (DEM epic).
title: Pebble beds: DEM -> packing -> CSG -> Monte Carlo workflow for a small agent

description: GH #37 §A. Vertex/edge/face select modes; box/circle/lasso region select; select all/none/invert; select linked (L, Ctrl+L) by connectivity and by seam/sharp/material/normal delimiter; select mirror. Headless: operators take an explicit selection set + predicate, return the new set. Foundation for every other Edit-Mode operator in this epic.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: src/selection.rs (new module, ~560 LOC + 10 tests). Selection{mode, verts/edges/faces sets}; SelectMode/Element/Axis/RegionMode enums. select/deselect/toggle/select_all/deselect_all/invert (mode-sensitive); set_mode with Blender selection-flush; union/subtract/intersect/retain set-algebra; select_in_box / select_in_sphere / select_in_screen_polygon (box+circle+lasso via a caller-supplied projector); select_linked / select_linked_from; select_mirror across an Axis plane. sync() re-derives the 2 non-active domains after every mutation. title: outram-blender: selection foundations (modes, box/circle/lasso, all/none/invert, linked)

description:
Found 2026-08-12 (op-62vf). Recorded as UNRESOLVED rather than guessed at.

SYMPTOM. With a saturated 7 MPa start, alpha_g = 1e-4 and a 10 um bubble diameter, the ramped blowdown survives 11 steps and then fails with:

  TAMPINES numerical failure: volume constraint alpha_g + alpha_l = 1 is violated by
  0.0012295274121916222 after 20 outer correctors at t = 0.00036 s, above the 1e-4 limit

i.e. the outer-corrector Newton iteration on the volume residual stops converging. The same configuration at 1 mm bubbles fails differently (the metastable-bound refusal, separate bead), and the 10 um run is otherwise BETTER behaved -- the phase-temperature difference falls from 49.8 K to 5.74 K, which is the interfacial closures working as intended.

WHAT IS KNOWN.
- The Newton system is the correct quasi-Jacobian: M = -(V/dt) dR/dp, assembled from the compliance C_i = sum_k alpha_k psi_k / rho_k on the diagonal and the pressure-corrected face fluxes off it. It is strictly diagonally dominant.
- The compressibilities psi_k are taken along the isentropic path (dh_k = dp/rho_k), which is the path the step actually takes; using the fixed-enthalpy derivative instead was measured to stall the correctors and was fixed on 2026-08-12.
- Under-relaxation is 0.7 and 20 correctors were allowed.

LEADING HYPOTHESIS, NOT VERIFIED. The residual R(p) is not smooth in p once the mass-transfer rate limiter (MAX_MASS_TRANSFER_FRACTION_PER_STEP) and the residual-alpha phase floor (PHASE_FLOOR_TRIGGER) switch on and off between correctors. Newton on a piecewise residual does not converge. The failing run showed those branches firing on most cells (lim = 22-24, floor = 30 of 24 cells over both stages). If that is right, the fix is to make the branch decisions once per STEP rather than once per corrector, or to smooth the limiter.

DO NOT paper over this by raising MAX_VOLUME_RESIDUAL. The refusal is correct: a step whose phases do not fill the cell to better than 1e-4 has not converged, and returning it would give a density field wrong by the residual.

NEXT STEP: instrument the corrector loop to print R and max|dp| per corrector for the failing step, and check whether the limiter/floor branch set changes between correctors.
title: tampines TwoFluid1d: outer-corrector Newton fails to converge the volume constraint at small bubble diameter -- UNDIAGNOSED

description:
Additive, non-breaking tensor/vector-field FV operators translated from vendored OpenFOAM (commit 481094fd), flagged blocking by the GeN-Foam thermo-mechanics port (op-p6p.11):

1. fvc::grad_vec: VolVectorField -> VolTensorField (Gauss grad, outer(Sf,u_f))
2. fvc::div_tensor: VolTensorField -> VolVectorField; fvc::div_symm_tensor: VolSymmTensorField -> VolVectorField (Gauss div, Sf & sigma_f)
3. fvm::d2dt2: implicit Euler 2nd time-derivative for VolVectorField -> FvVectorMatrix
4. fvm::Sp / fvm::Su / fvm::su_sp: implicit + explicit source terms (scalar & vector)
5. Field-level tensor algebra: tr/symm/two_symm/dev/dev2 on VolTensorField/VolSymmTensorField

Translated from src/finiteVolume/finiteVolume/{fvc/fvcGrad,fvc/fvcDiv,fvm/fvmSup,fvm/fvmD2dt2} + gaussGrad/gaussDivScheme/EulerD2dt2Scheme. V&V tests: grad(A.x)=A^T, div(linear tensor)=known const, d2dt2(quadratic-in-t)=const. Unblocks op-p6p.11 (deferred GeN-Foam thermoMechanics/TH mesh solves).

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
DONE 2026-07-15. Added (all additive, non-breaking):
fvc::grad_vec (VolVectorField->VolTensorField, gaussGrad outer(Sf,u_f)); fvc::div_tensor + fvc::div_symm_tensor (Vol[Symm]TensorField->VolVectorField, gaussDivScheme Sf&sigma); fvm::d2dt2 + d2dt2_coeff (VolVectorField ->FvVectorMatrix, EulerD2dt2Scheme, constant-dt); fvm::{sp,su,su_sp,sp_vec,su_vec,su_sp_vec} (fvmSup, OpenFOAM signs: Sp diag+=V*sp, Su source-=V*su); fields::vol_field_algebra::{tr,tr_of_symm,symm,two_symm,two_symm_of_symm,dev,dev2,dev_of_symm,dev2_of_symm}. Added PatchField::{zero_gradient_tensor,fixed_value_tensor,zero_gradient_symm_tensor,fixed_value_symm_tensor}. 13 new V&V tests, all pass (grad(A.x)=A^T; div(linear tensor)=x-row of M; d2dt2(quadratic-in-t)=2c; Sp/Su solve k.phi=S). cargo test -p outram-foam-basic-lib --lib --release: 245 passed 0 failed 4 ignored. Android aarch64-linux-android check clean. clippy clean on new files. No existing public signatures changed. Unblocks op-p6p.11 (GeN-Foam thermoMechanics DEqn/TEqn). Follow-up for op-p6p.11: no fvm::laplacian(tensor-coeff) or explicit non-orthogonal correction; grad_vec is single Gauss pass; d2dt2 assumes constant dt + non-moving mesh (no V0/V00 history in FvMesh).

title: Tensor/vector FV operators for GeN-Foam thermoMechanics (unblocks op-p6p.11)
